Toxic Streaming

By: Graham Coetzer | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
He made a living from streaming chaos and violence—now he's behind bars, accused of murder; has influencer culture gone too far?

Unique Selling Point:
Ruan Beetge and Gordon Westraad are currently behind bars, pending their ongoing bail application. The men stand accused of th murder after 27-year-old father Brandon Pretorius from Jansen Park. This after they allegedly beat him up outside the Malbroer Pub and Grill in Boksburg. Pretorius succumbed to his injuries on the 6th of May this year, several days after he was hospitalised following the alleged beating. But Ruan Beetge is no stranger to violence. He's a relatively well known streamer amongst the Afrikaans TikTok social media community. And during live streams Beetge regularly hosted, he bragged about how beating people up not only gained him a significant following on the popular app, it also made him money.

Meanwhile, the Malbroer Pub and Grill is also owned by Pascal Kaci, the same owner as the Latinos Bistro which we've previously reported on. According to our sources Pascal was not involved in any way, but it cannot be ignored that yet another death has occurred outside a pub he owns.

Summary:
There is a dark half to the Afrikaans side of TikTok, one where "drama lives" - live streaming where influencers expose, degrade and generally air their dirty laundry - have reached dangerous heights. In the past few months, streamers have threatened each other, made and received death threats, and even attempted suicide during live streams. But Beetge grew his following after he got into a fist fight with another popular streamer during a live stream. And this is not just a claim other are making, he's said as much during his live streams. The fight got him enough attention and followers to start his own live streaming, during which followers can "gift" streamers cash donations. Beetge's streams mostly involved him bragging about how he would beat up people on weekends, and apparently gained him enough money to make a living from streaming.

That all seems to have come to abrupt and tragic end after the fight with Brandon Pretorius outside the Malbroer Pub. Is this a case of social media fantasy turning into real world tragedy?

Further information:
There are ample TikTok videos available showing Beetge bragging about making money from fights, behaving badly etc.
While some members of the public spoke out about his behaviour on social media, many more followed and supported him.
There is some CCTV footage available of the fight that took place outside Malbroer in the parking lot.
Brandon's family are willing to speak to us.
Popular Afrikaans Tiktoker Juan Melvin has some videos etc to share, and understands the TikTok culture well. He's been covering the case on his lives for the past few weeks and is willing to speak to us.

Script:


(Cell Phone Video Singing) Happy birthday to you…



(Cell Phone Video Singing) Happy birthday, dear Brandon…



(Lourensa) A family celebration in Boksburg on Johannesburg’s East Rand.



(Cell Phone Video Singing) Happy birthday to you. Hip-hip, hooray!



(Lourensa) Increasingly known for its brutal nightlife, it’s a place where the young father in this video crossed paths with a man notorious for violence.



(Ruan Beetge Subtitles) Ruan 3 verse 4. I’m going to p**sklap Christiaan. Ruan 3 verse 4. Hear me.



(Ruan Beetge Subtitles) G*d. Guys, I’m going to lose my sh*t. I’m going to lose my sh*t.



(Lourensa) These days, it seems as though every other person wants to be a social media influencer. And it’s understandable because it brings fame and fortune. But the lengths that some people will go to could have deadly consequences.



(Juan Melvin) TikTok; they thrive on the drama. And the more drama, the more gifting.



(Lourensa) Juan Melvin is a businessman, wildlife activist and popular content creator on TikTok, the country’s third largest social media platform.



(Lourensa) Like many Afrikaans influencers, he’s built a large following through interactive live streams. Some make good money.



(Lourensa) How much money are we talking here?



(Juan Melvin) The average Joe makes between R3000 and R4000 a month. And then you get your people that easily… I mean, back in the days when we had the weekly ranking, I remember a group of people that cashed out R330 000. For a week rank, ja.



(Juan Melvin Subtitles) So, the bail application is just postponed.



(Lourensa) Followers can donate funds to their favourite live streamers by paying for virtual gifts, which can then be cashed in for real world money. Streamers compete against each other to earn the most gifts from their followers which, in turn, increases their ranking. It seems, to make it big on Afrikaans TikTok, drama is a key ingredient.



(Man 1 Subtitles) You’re sitting in a club on a Wednesday you unemployed piece of n**i. Voetsek!



(Ruan Beetge Subtitles) My friend, I still make more in two days than you get paid in a week. So, p**s off!





(Lourensa) It’s an often primitive and angry space where people like Ruan Beetge, an unemployed 30-year-old, thrive. His TikTok claim to fame? His violent temper.



(Man 1 Subtitles) The only thing Ruan beats up is women and people smaller than him. But he never hits men.



(Ruan Beetge Subtitles) You carry on like a b*tch because I p**sklapped you as well. You’re dead right, you f**king little girl.



(Lourensa) Ruan didn’t hide his violent nature online; he thrived on it. And his antics were well known to the TikTok community. He used the platform to bully and threaten.



(Juan Melvin) I saw signs very early on when I got to see him on TikTok. And I did warn a few people and said stay away. Because he made threats to one of my friends. And I phoned my friend, and I said, “Listen, from this guy you stay away. It won’t end well.”



(Lourensa) Far from staying away, his followers tuned in for the violence.



(Ruan Beetge Subtitles) I wanted to knee you!



(Lourensa) And he often bragged about just how much his brand of chaos was worth.



(Ruan Beetge Subtitles) It was a Sunday night. I started ranking that Sunday night. I did 688 000 coins in seven hours.



(Lourensa) Which means that streaming his toxic behaviour had been worth between R80 000 and R100 000 in just a few short hours.



(Juan Melvin) So, you can make easy money. You know, the more drama, the more evil, the more gruesome, the more money.



(Lourensa) So, the worst of the worst go to TikTok?



(Juan Melvin) There’s more of people that shouldn’t be allowed to have a phone in my opinion.



(Ruan Beetge Subtitles) But I thought it would count each time I fight, so then I fought in the parking lots weekly. And people didn’t pay me. Now, my hands are f*cked and my bank account is empty.



(Lourensa) Then, in the early hours of a Saturday morning in late April, the chaos Ruan cultivated online spilled into the real world after an altercation, caught on CCTV camera.



(Lourensa) A family has been left shattered, and a young girl fatherless.



(Lisa Pretorius) He liked to stay at home, watch DVDs or have a braai at home, entertain people at home, you know, and play pool and that type of thing.



(Lourensa) We spoke to Brandon Pretorius’s mom, Lisa in one of his favourite rooms. It’s where he played pool in a house he shared with his parents, his siblings, his girlfriend and his young daughter, Mila.



(Lourensa) How was he as a father?



(Lisa Pretorius) Oh, he adored her. It was like his life, ja.



(Lourensa) How was it like for you as a mother to see him as a father?



(Lisa Pretorius) I thought that he would be like that. Entertain her and spoil her. Ja, no… He was a wonderful dad. No, he was.



(Lourensa) On that weekend in April, Brandon and his girlfriend had joined his sister, Haydi for a night of celebration.



(Lourensa) So, what happened on that night when you guys went out? It was your birthday?



(Haydi Pretorius) Yes. Nothing really happened. We were all happy and, you know, everything was normal. But we left early… Earlier, like an hour earlier before it happened.



(Lourensa) It’s not exactly clear what happened after Haydi left and the events are currently the subject of a court case. But here’s what we do know: Brandon’s group spent the night at a popular local club called Malbroer.



(Lourensa) Ruan Beetge was also there - this is a picture of him allegedly taken that night. Crucially, Brandon had left his phone at home.



(Juan Melvin) His daughter, little daughter played with the phone and that locked the phone. And then he left the phone by his dad. So, he never took a phone with to the club.



(Lourensa) According to court testimony, Ruan says at some point that night, Brandon touched his girlfriend inappropriately and stole her cell phone.



(Juan Melvin) Brandon was then asked to leave the club by the bouncers, which he did. And he went and he stood outside.



(Lourensa) The CCTV footage shows Brandon leaving the club just before 2 o’clock in the morning, where it’s likely he waited for his girlfriend.



(Juan Melvin) The girlfriend in the meantime, Brandon’s girlfriend, thinks that he’s still in the bathroom.



(Lourensa) Moments later, Ruan appears in the parking lot and, without any visible provocation, he attacks Brandon.



(Juan Melvin) Ruan comes out, and he knocks him with a lefty and he knocks him flat out. And you can see there is some altercation happening while he’s on the ground.



(Lourensa) Brandon was eventually able to get up and make his way to his car.



(Juan Melvin) He’s on his way home now to tell his dad, “Listen, I can’t get in, you know. My girlfriend is still inside.”



(Lourensa) So, after the incident in the parking lot, Brandon Pretorius drove down this road. It’s dark and deserted, and this is where his father found his near-lifeless body.



(Lourensa) We know that Brandon’s car never made it past this corner, just a few hundred meters from the club. We also know his car was in some kind of accident. And it’s alleged he was later followed here by multiple attackers – one of those allegedly Ruan Beetge – before being assaulted again.



(Lourensa) In a statement, Malbroer’s management said they were not in any way associated with the incident and stands firmly against any form of violence.



(Lourensa) When did you get the call?



(Lisa Pretorius) Well, I got the call in the early hours of the morning because I was watching Mila. So, ja, the tow truck driver called me. And I was the last number that he gave this man. I was the last thing he said. And then, he didn’t speak again.



(Lourensa) After losing consciousness at the scene, Brandon was rushed to hospital where he spent several days fighting for this life.



(Lisa Pretorius) The neurologist came in and she said they have to open and do this and that. And it was a seven-hour operation. But it didn’t look well after that. There was still no movement, nothing.



(Cell Phone Video Singing) Happy birthday to you…



(Lourensa) A little more than a week later, a day after his own birthday, Brandon died.



(Lourensa) Why do you think they did this to Brandon?



(Lisa Pretorius) We still don’t know. I know it’s not a cellphone or touching his girlfriend. Because he just got a new cellphone and Mila just blocked it. She was playing a game on it, so why would he? We still don’t know. I would still like to find out what the real story was.



(Mark Gilpin) So, he moves from one club to another club to another club, and looks for nonsense with the people in the clubs and that. Just for the social media. And it’s not fair to the other parties involved.



(Lourensa) Mark Gilpin is from the Boksburg North Community Policing Forum. He joined us as we revisited the spot near where Brandon’s car had come to a stop.



(Lourensa) Something did happen here?



(Mark Gilpin) Yes, ja. You can see definitely, he’s got a maroon car and there’s the maroon colours of the car on the pole still. And there’s a photo of his…



(Lourensa) This is him and his daughter.



(Mark Gilpin) Him and his daughter, ja.



(Lourensa) But was Ruan known in the area for causing trouble?



(Mark Gilpin) All over, he was known. So, that’s why he’s been banned at most of the clubs in Boksburg North. They have banned him from entering their premises.



(Lourensa) Why?



(Mark Gilpin) Because of fighting. The bottom line is fighting.



(Ruan Beetge Subtitles) I’m going to lose my sh*t.



(Lourensa) Clips like this one, showing Ruan livestreaming on TikTok after yet another apparent fight, are still surfacing. It’s not hard to see why he’s been banned from so many venues.



(Ruan Beetge Subtitles) It’s just my hands. It’s just my hands that are full of blood. And my head. And now my arms. But I’m fine.



(Lourensa) But in the days after Brandon’s death, police were slow to react. Desperate for justice, the family asked Juan to use social media to shine a light on the case.



(Juan Melvin) It didn’t sound like they got justice because they didn’t know who the investigating officer was, is it going to change, who to send details to. They didn’t get the answers that they wanted.



(Lourensa) As speculation about Ruan’s involvement spread across social media, he went live one last time.



(Ruan Beetge Subtitles) Now, obviously, there’s an incident that everyone’s talking about that took place.



(Lourensa) As he spoke, his followers were still sending likes on his stream.



(Ruan Beetge Subtitles) I’m unfortunately not going to talk about this case in my live. It is a legal matter. And anything I say here, or whatever I do, can be used against me.



(Lourensa) Last month, Ruan Beetge and his co-accused, Gordon Westraad handed themselves to the police. Charged with murder, they will remain behind bars until their ongoing bail application is finalised. His legal team says he will plead not guilty. Brandon’s family has been in court.



(Lisa Pretorius) I don’t know, he mustn’t see the outside of jail, he must stay there forever. Like, they must still feel what this poor child of mine had to go through.



(Lourensa) The court has heard about three previous assault charges against Ruan - one a case of domestic violence - but they were withdrawn.



(Lourensa) How has it been for his daughter?



(Haydi Pretorius) It’s really sad hearing her call her dad and knowing he won’t come back.



(Lourensa) A culture of violence spurred on by a lust for social media likes appear to lie at the heart of this tragedy. Now, a little girl will grow up without a father.



(Lourensa) And a mother will grow old without a son.



(Lisa Pretorius) I just miss him so much. You wait for him to just walk through the door.

mihle@combinedartists.co.za 16 June 2025 TX Date: 0000-00-00 Script: (Cell Phone Video Singing) Happy birthday to you… (Cell Phone Video Singing) Happy birthday, dear Brandon… (Lourensa) A family celebration in Boksburg on Johannesburg’s East Rand. (Cell Phone Video Singing) Happy birthday to you. Hip-hip, hooray! (Lourensa) Increasingly known for its brutal nightlife, it’s a place where the young father in this video crossed paths with a man notorious for violence. (Ruan Beetge Subtitles) Ruan 3 verse 4. I’m going to p**sklap Christiaan. Ruan 3 verse 4. Hear me. (Ruan Beetge Subtitles) G*d. Guys, I’m going to lose my sh*t. I’m going to lose my sh*t. (Lourensa) These days, it seems as though every other person wants to be a social media influencer. And it’s understandable because it brings fame and fortune. But the lengths that some people will go to could have deadly consequences. (Juan Melvin) TikTok; they thrive on the drama. And the more drama, the more gifting. (Lourensa) Juan Melvin is a businessman, wildlife activist and popular content creator on TikTok, the country’s third largest social media platform. (Lourensa) Like many Afrikaans influencers, he’s built a large following through interactive live streams. Some make good money. (Lourensa) How much money are we talking here? (Juan Melvin) The average Joe makes between R3000 and R4000 a month. And then you get your people that easily… I mean, back in the days when we had the weekly ranking, I remember a group of people that cashed out R330 000. For a week rank, ja. (Juan Melvin Subtitles) So, the bail application is just postponed. (Lourensa) Followers can donate funds to their favourite live streamers by paying for virtual gifts, which can then be cashed in for real world money. Streamers compete against each other to earn the most gifts from their followers which, in turn, increases their ranking. It seems, to make it big on Afrikaans TikTok, drama is a key ingredient. (Man 1 Subtitles) You’re sitting in a club on a Wednesday you unemployed piece of n**i. Voetsek! (Ruan Beetge Subtitles) My friend, I still make more in two days than you get paid in a week. So, p**s off! (Lourensa) It’s an often primitive and angry space where people like Ruan Beetge, an unemployed 30-year-old, thrive. His TikTok claim to fame? His violent temper. (Man 1 Subtitles) The only thing Ruan beats up is women and people smaller than him. But he never hits men. (Ruan Beetge Subtitles) You carry on like a b*tch because I p**sklapped you as well. You’re dead right, you f**king little girl. (Lourensa) Ruan didn’t hide his violent nature online; he thrived on it. And his antics were well known to the TikTok community. He used the platform to bully and threaten. (Juan Melvin) I saw signs very early on when I got to see him on TikTok. And I did warn a few people and said stay away. Because he made threats to one of my friends. And I phoned my friend, and I said, “Listen, from this guy you stay away. It won’t end well.” (Lourensa) Far from staying away, his followers tuned in for the violence. (Ruan Beetge Subtitles) I wanted to knee you! (Lourensa) And he often bragged about just how much his brand of chaos was worth. (Ruan Beetge Subtitles) It was a Sunday night. I started ranking that Sunday night. I did 688 000 coins in seven hours. (Lourensa) Which means that streaming his toxic behaviour had been worth between R80 000 and R100 000 in just a few short hours. (Juan Melvin) So, you can make easy money. You know, the more drama, the more evil, the more gruesome, the more money. (Lourensa) So, the worst of the worst go to TikTok? (Juan Melvin) There’s more of people that shouldn’t be allowed to have a phone in my opinion. (Ruan Beetge Subtitles) But I thought it would count each time I fight, so then I fought in the parking lots weekly. And people didn’t pay me. Now, my hands are f*cked and my bank account is empty. (Lourensa) Then, in the early hours of a Saturday morning in late April, the chaos Ruan cultivated online spilled into the real world after an altercation, caught on CCTV camera. (Lourensa) A family has been left shattered, and a young girl fatherless. (Lisa Pretorius) He liked to stay at home, watch DVDs or have a braai at home, entertain people at home, you know, and play pool and that type of thing. (Lourensa) We spoke to Brandon Pretorius’s mom, Lisa in one of his favourite rooms. It’s where he played pool in a house he shared with his parents, his siblings, his girlfriend and his young daughter, Mila. (Lourensa) How was he as a father? (Lisa Pretorius) Oh, he adored her. It was like his life, ja. (Lourensa) How was it like for you as a mother to see him as a father? (Lisa Pretorius) I thought that he would be like that. Entertain her and spoil her. Ja, no… He was a wonderful dad. No, he was. (Lourensa) On that weekend in April, Brandon and his girlfriend had joined his sister, Haydi for a night of celebration. (Lourensa) So, what happened on that night when you guys went out? It was your birthday? (Haydi Pretorius) Yes. Nothing really happened. We were all happy and, you know, everything was normal. But we left early… Earlier, like an hour earlier before it happened. (Lourensa) It’s not exactly clear what happened after Haydi left and the events are currently the subject of a court case. But here’s what we do know: Brandon’s group spent the night at a popular local club called Malbroer. (Lourensa) Ruan Beetge was also there - this is a picture of him allegedly taken that night. Crucially, Brandon had left his phone at home. (Juan Melvin) His daughter, little daughter played with the phone and that locked the phone. And then he left the phone by his dad. So, he never took a phone with to the club. (Lourensa) According to court testimony, Ruan says at some point that night, Brandon touched his girlfriend inappropriately and stole her cell phone. (Juan Melvin) Brandon was then asked to leave the club by the bouncers, which he did. And he went and he stood outside. (Lourensa) The CCTV footage shows Brandon leaving the club just before 2 o’clock in the morning, where it’s likely he waited for his girlfriend. (Juan Melvin) The girlfriend in the meantime, Brandon’s girlfriend, thinks that he’s still in the bathroom. (Lourensa) Moments later, Ruan appears in the parking lot and, without any visible provocation, he attacks Brandon. (Juan Melvin) Ruan comes out, and he knocks him with a lefty and he knocks him flat out. And you can see there is some altercation happening while he’s on the ground. (Lourensa) Brandon was eventually able to get up and make his way to his car. (Juan Melvin) He’s on his way home now to tell his dad, “Listen, I can’t get in, you know. My girlfriend is still inside.” (Lourensa) So, after the incident in the parking lot, Brandon Pretorius drove down this road. It’s dark and deserted, and this is where his father found his near-lifeless body. (Lourensa) We know that Brandon’s car never made it past this corner, just a few hundred meters from the club. We also know his car was in some kind of accident. And it’s alleged he was later followed here by multiple attackers – one of those allegedly Ruan Beetge – before being assaulted again. (Lourensa) In a statement, Malbroer’s management said they were not in any way associated with the incident and stands firmly against any form of violence. (Lourensa) When did you get the call? (Lisa Pretorius) Well, I got the call in the early hours of the morning because I was watching Mila. So, ja, the tow truck driver called me. And I was the last number that he gave this man. I was the last thing he said. And then, he didn’t speak again. (Lourensa) After losing consciousness at the scene, Brandon was rushed to hospital where he spent several days fighting for this life. (Lisa Pretorius) The neurologist came in and she said they have to open and do this and that. And it was a seven-hour operation. But it didn’t look well after that. There was still no movement, nothing. (Cell Phone Video Singing) Happy birthday to you… (Lourensa) A little more than a week later, a day after his own birthday, Brandon died. (Lourensa) Why do you think they did this to Brandon? (Lisa Pretorius) We still don’t know. I know it’s not a cellphone or touching his girlfriend. Because he just got a new cellphone and Mila just blocked it. She was playing a game on it, so why would he? We still don’t know. I would still like to find out what the real story was. (Mark Gilpin) So, he moves from one club to another club to another club, and looks for nonsense with the people in the clubs and that. Just for the social media. And it’s not fair to the other parties involved. (Lourensa) Mark Gilpin is from the Boksburg North Community Policing Forum. He joined us as we revisited the spot near where Brandon’s car had come to a stop. (Lourensa) Something did happen here? (Mark Gilpin) Yes, ja. You can see definitely, he’s got a maroon car and there’s the maroon colours of the car on the pole still. And there’s a photo of his… (Lourensa) This is him and his daughter. (Mark Gilpin) Him and his daughter, ja. (Lourensa) But was Ruan known in the area for causing trouble? (Mark Gilpin) All over, he was known. So, that’s why he’s been banned at most of the clubs in Boksburg North. They have banned him from entering their premises. (Lourensa) Why? (Mark Gilpin) Because of fighting. The bottom line is fighting. (Ruan Beetge Subtitles) I’m going to lose my sh*t. (Lourensa) Clips like this one, showing Ruan livestreaming on TikTok after yet another apparent fight, are still surfacing. It’s not hard to see why he’s been banned from so many venues. (Ruan Beetge Subtitles) It’s just my hands. It’s just my hands that are full of blood. And my head. And now my arms. But I’m fine. (Lourensa) But in the days after Brandon’s death, police were slow to react. Desperate for justice, the family asked Juan to use social media to shine a light on the case. (Juan Melvin) It didn’t sound like they got justice because they didn’t know who the investigating officer was, is it going to change, who to send details to. They didn’t get the answers that they wanted. (Lourensa) As speculation about Ruan’s involvement spread across social media, he went live one last time. (Ruan Beetge Subtitles) Now, obviously, there’s an incident that everyone’s talking about that took place. (Lourensa) As he spoke, his followers were still sending likes on his stream. (Ruan Beetge Subtitles) I’m unfortunately not going to talk about this case in my live. It is a legal matter. And anything I say here, or whatever I do, can be used against me. (Lourensa) Last month, Ruan Beetge and his co-accused, Gordon Westraad handed themselves to the police. Charged with murder, they will remain behind bars until their ongoing bail application is finalised. His legal team says he will plead not guilty. Brandon’s family has been in court. (Lisa Pretorius) I don’t know, he mustn’t see the outside of jail, he must stay there forever. Like, they must still feel what this poor child of mine had to go through. (Lourensa) The court has heard about three previous assault charges against Ruan - one a case of domestic violence - but they were withdrawn. (Lourensa) How has it been for his daughter? (Haydi Pretorius) It’s really sad hearing her call her dad and knowing he won’t come back. (Lourensa) A culture of violence spurred on by a lust for social media likes appear to lie at the heart of this tragedy. Now, a little girl will grow up without a father. (Lourensa) And a mother will grow old without a son. (Lisa Pretorius) I just miss him so much. You wait for him to just walk through the door.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): He made a living from streaming chaos and violence—now he's behind bars, accused of murder; has influencer culture gone too far?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Ruan Beetge and Gordon Westraad are currently behind bars, pending their ongoing bail application. The men stand accused of th murder after 27-year-old father Brandon Pretorius from Jansen Park. This after they allegedly beat him up outside the Malbroer Pub and Grill in Boksburg. Pretorius succumbed to his injuries on the 6th of May this year, several days after he was hospitalised following the alleged beating. But Ruan Beetge is no stranger to violence. He's a relatively well known streamer amongst the Afrikaans TikTok social media community. And during live streams Beetge regularly hosted, he bragged about how beating people up not only gained him a significant following on the popular app, it also made him money. Meanwhile, the Malbroer Pub and Grill is also owned by Pascal Kaci, the same owner as the Latinos Bistro which we've previously reported on. According to our sources Pascal was not involved in any way, but it cannot be ignored that yet another death has occurred outside a pub he owns.
metadata.Summary: There is a dark half to the Afrikaans side of TikTok, one where "drama lives" - live streaming where influencers expose, degrade and generally air their dirty laundry - have reached dangerous heights. In the past few months, streamers have threatened each other, made and received death threats, and even attempted suicide during live streams. But Beetge grew his following after he got into a fist fight with another popular streamer during a live stream. And this is not just a claim other are making, he's said as much during his live streams. The fight got him enough attention and followers to start his own live streaming, during which followers can "gift" streamers cash donations. Beetge's streams mostly involved him bragging about how he would beat up people on weekends, and apparently gained him enough money to make a living from streaming. That all seems to have come to abrupt and tragic end after the fight with Brandon Pretorius outside the Malbroer Pub. Is this a case of social media fantasy turning into real world tragedy?
metadata.Further information: There are ample TikTok videos available showing Beetge bragging about making money from fights, behaving badly etc. While some members of the public spoke out about his behaviour on social media, many more followed and supported him. There is some CCTV footage available of the fight that took place outside Malbroer in the parking lot. Brandon's family are willing to speak to us. Popular Afrikaans Tiktoker Juan Melvin has some videos etc to share, and understands the TikTok culture well. He's been covering the case on his lives for the past few weeks and is willing to speak to us.
